layers.note: A bunchgrass of open desert, grassland and prairie.

moisture.note: Dry hills and plains (Hitchcock; Kearney and Peebles).

elevation_m.note: 305 to 1,525 m in Arizona (FEIS); up to 5,000 feet (Kearney and Peebles); higher further north.

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about −12 to 14 °C; gone below −18 °C and above 18 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −34 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −40 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 20 to 32 °C; gone below 17 °C, where summers are too short, and above 35 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 3,000 to 9,000 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 2,200.

degree_days_5.note: About 1,500 to 7,000 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 1,000.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.06 to 0.8, gone by 0.03 and above 1.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit: it also grows where winter rain dominates, as in the Mojave Desert; where the monsoon brings summer rain, as on the bajada, up to about 0.8 of the year's precipitation in summer, gone by 0.9.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Saguaro desert scene (the west bajada of Saguaro National Park's Tucson Mountain District, about 750 m, 32.25 N 111.17 W) from general knowledge of the species and the ranges, habitats and elevations in the sources read for its spec (2026-10-19). Purple threeawn grows from the Great Plains (Arkansas and Kansas) to Utah, Arizona, southern California and northern Mexico (FEIS; Hitchcock; Kearney and Peebles). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records; every full range holds the bajada's climate (coldest month about 11 °C, warmest about 31 °C, about 7,600 degree-days above 0 °C, coldest night about −4 °C, moisture index about 0.15, about half the year's rain in summer).
